records.label: spacr.zstack#5
records.source: **Stitching 2-D planes is not 3-D segmentation.** Both are legitimate and they give different answers. Per-plane segmentation followed by IoU linking (:data:`MODE_STITCH`) sees each plane independently and cannot recover an object that is invisible in one plane; true volumetric segmentation (:data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC`) uses the z gradient but is far more sensitive to a wrong anisotropy. The mode is therefore explicit, never inferred, and :class:`ZStackResult` records which one actually ran so it can be written next to the numbers it produced.
records.context: **Stitching 2-D image layers is not 3-D segmentation.** Both are legitimate and they give different answers. Per-image-layer segmentation followed by IoU linking (:data:`MODE_STITCH`) sees each image layer independently and cannot recover an object that is invisible in one image layer; true volumetric segmentation (:data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC`) uses the z gradient but is far more sensitive to a wrong anisotropy. The mode is therefore explicit, never inferred, and :class:`ZStackResult` records which one actually ran so it can be written next to the numbers it produced.
records.translation: **Samsetning 2-D myndarlaga er ekki 3-D skiptun.** Bæði eru lögleg og þau gefa mismunandi svör. Skiptun á hverju myndalagi ásamt IoU tengingu (:data:`MODE_STITCH`) skoðar hvert myndalag sjálfstætt og getur ekki endurheimt hlut sem er ósýnilegur í einu myndalagi; raunveruleg rúmmáls-skiptun (:data:`MODE_VOLUMETRIC`) notar z-hallann en er mun næmari fyrir röngum ósamhverfun. Hátt er því skýrt, aldrei ályktað, og :class:`ZStackResult` skráir hvaða aðferð var raunverulega keyrð svo hægt sé að skrifa það við hliðina á tölunum sem hún framleiddi.

records.label: spacr.power_simulate#19
records.source: **Sequencing error** (:func:`misassign_reads`, ``sequencing_error_rate=``). Both packages treat the read fraction as an exact record of which genotypes were in a well. Substitution errors, index hopping, PCR chimeras and mismatch-tolerant demultiplexing all credit reads to the wrong gene. Simulating it says the direct dilution is small — but that it silently disables the unidentified-gene check, turning genes that were correctly reported as untested into confident non-hits. On the reference design that costs ten times more than the dilution does. See :func:`misassign_reads`.
records.context: **Sequencing error** (:func:`misassign_reads`, ``sequencing_error_rate=``). Both packages treat the read fraction as an exact record of which genotypes were in a microplate sample position. Substitution errors, index hopping, PCR chimeras and mismatch-tolerant demultiplexing all credit reads to the wrong gene. Simulating it says the direct dilution is small — but that it silently disables the unidentified-gene check, turning genes that were correctly reported as untested into confident non-hits. On the reference design that costs ten times more than the dilution does. See :func:`misassign_reads`.
records.translation: **Röðunarvilla** (:func:`misassign_reads`, ``sequencing_error_rate=``). Bæði pakkarnir meðhöndla lesna hlutann sem nákvæmt skrá yfir hvaða genatýpur voru í sýnatöflu í örplötu. Staðsetningavillur, skiptivísis hopp, PCR kirma og ósamræmi-tollandi fjöldagreining umbúna lesur á rangt gen. Hermun segir að bein þynning sé lítil — en það slekkur hljóðlega á athugun á óþekktum genum og breytir genum sem rétt voru skráð sem óprófuð í örugg að ekki hafi fundist áhrif. Á viðmiðunahönnuninni kostar það tíu sinnum meira en þynningin gerir. Sjá :func:`misassign_reads`.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#19
records.source: **The threshold is a stated false-positive rate, not a tuned fraction.** Under multivariate normality the squared robust Mahalanobis distance is distributed chi-square with ``p`` degrees of freedom, so the cut point is ``chi2.ppf(1 - alpha, p)`` for a chosen ``alpha`` — default :data:`DEFAULT_ALPHA` = 0.001, meaning *one clean object in a thousand is expected to be flagged*. Over 10^5 objects that is about 100 false flags, and over the 200,000 objects of a typical two-plate screen it is about 200. That number is knowable in advance and is printed in :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats`. An isolation forest's score has no such null distribution and therefore no calibrated cut point at all.
records.context: **The threshold is a stated false-positive rate, not a tuned fraction.** Under multivariate normality the squared robust Mahalanobis distance is distributed chi-square with ``p`` degrees of freedom, so the cut point is ``chi2.ppf(1 - alpha, p)`` for a chosen ``alpha`` — default :data:`DEFAULT_ALPHA` = 0.001, meaning *one clean object in a thousand is expected to be flagged*. Over 10^5 objects that is about 100 false flags, and over the 200,000 objects of a typical two-plate screen it is about 200. That number is knowable in advance and is printed in :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats`. An isolation forest's score has no such null distribution and therefore no calibrated cut point at all.
records.translation: **Þröskuldurinn er tilgreindur falskur-jákvæður hlutfall, ekki stilltur hluti.** Við margbreytilega normaldreifingu er kvaðratið af stöðugum Mahalanobis-fjarlægðinni dreift sem kvaðratrót með ``p`` frjálsum stigum, svo skurðpunkturinn er ``chi2.ppf(1 - alpha, p)`` fyrir valið ``alpha`` — sjálfgefið :data:`DEFAULT_ALPHA` = 0,001, sem þýðir *einn hreinn hlutur af þúsund er búist við að verði merktur*. Yfir 10^5 hlutum eru það um 100 falskar merkingar, og yfir 200.000 hlutum sem eru í dæmigerðu tveggja-platta skjá sem er um 200. Sá fjöldi er þekktur fyrirfram og er prentaður í :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats`. Stig aðskilnaðar skógar hefur enga slíka núll-dreifingu og því engan stilltan skurðpunkt yfirhöfuð.

records.label: spacr.omero.measurement_pairs#2
records.source: **Why there is a cap.** A spaCR object table has 300-600 columns. A MapAnnotation with 400 entries renders in OMERO.web as a 400-row scrolling table in a 300 px panel, which nobody reads and which makes the panel useless for the annotations that *were* worth showing. So the annotation is a *summary*, capped at ``max_pairs`` (:data:`MAX_MAP_PAIRS` = 50 by default) and ordered so the useful keys are the ones that survive: ``priority`` keys first in the order given, then the row's own order. When anything is cut, the last pair is :data:`TRUNCATION_KEY`, saying how many were dropped and that the full table is the CSV attached under :data:`NS_FILE`. The full table is never *only* in the annotation.
records.context: **Why there is a cap.** A spaCR object table has 300-600 columns. A MapAnnotation with 400 entries renders in OMERO.web as a 400-row scrolling table in a 300 px panel, which nobody reads and which makes the panel useless for the annotations that *were* worth showing. So the annotation is a *summary*, capped at ``max_pairs`` (:data:`MAX_MAP_PAIRS` = 50 by default) and ordered so the useful structured-data names are the ones that survive: ``priority`` structured-data names first in the order given, then the row's own order. When anything is cut, the last pair is :data:`TRUNCATION_KEY`, saying how many were dropped and that the full table is the CSV attached under :data:`NS_FILE`. The full table is never *only* in the annotation.
records.translation: **Af hverju það er hámark.** Tafla af spaCR hlutum hefur 300-600 dálka. Kortamerking með 400 færslum birtist í OMERO.web sem 400-raðar rennibraut í 300 px spjaldi, sem enginn les og gerir spjaldið gagnslaust fyrir þau athugasemdir sem *voru* þess virði að sýna. Þannig að athugasemdin er *yfirlit*, hámarkað við ``max_pairs`` (:data:`MAX_MAP_PAIRS` = 50 sjálfgefið) og raðað þannig að gagnleg nöfn á uppbyggðum gögnum eru þau sem lifa af: ``priority`` nöfn á uppbyggðum gögnum fyrst í gefnu röðinni, síðan röð raðarinnar sjálfrar. Þegar eitthvað er skorið niður, er síðasta parið :data:`TRUNCATION_KEY`, sem segir hversu mörg voru felld og að sú fulla tafla er CSV meðfylgjandi undir :data:`NS_FILE`. Sú fulla tafla er aldrei *aðeins* í athugasemdinni.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#30
records.source: The well pass reduces each well to a robust summary — the **median** of each feature over the well's objects, plus ``n`` — and then runs *the same* rule (:data:`METHOD_MAD`, :data:`METHOD_IQR` or :data:`METHOD_MAHALANOBIS`) across wells. The median rather than the mean for the same reason as everywhere else here: a single blown-up object must not become a bad well.
records.context: The well pass reduces each well to a robust summary — the **median** of each feature over the well's objects, plus ``n`` — and then runs *the same* rule (:data:`METHOD_MAD`, :data:`METHOD_IQR` or :data:`METHOD_MAHALANOBIS`) across microplate sample positions. The median rather than the mean for the same reason as everywhere else here: a single blown-up object must not become a bad well.
records.translation: Brunnagöngin minnkar hvern brunn niður í traustan samantekt — **miðgildi** hvers eiginleika yfir hlutina í brunninum, auk ``n`` — og keyrir síðan *sama* reglu (:data:`METHOD_MAD`, :data:`METHOD_IQR` eða :data:`METHOD_MAHALANOBIS`) yfir sýnistaði á örlögnum. Miðgildið frekar en meðaltalið er af sömu ástæðu og annars staðar hér: einn ofvaxinn hlutur má ekki verða að slæmum brunni.

records.label: spacr.cli.Module#10
records.source: ``"module:function"`` of a defaults helper that does **not** live in :mod:`spacr.settings`. Six built-in pipelines keep their own (``foreign``, ``external_masks``, ``convert``, ``illumination``, ``barcode_qc``, ``anndata_export``), as does every plugin app, because their keys are theirs alone; without this the CLI would resolve an empty defaults dict for them, and ``--set`` would then reject every one of their keys as a setting that does not exist.
records.context: ``"module:function"`` of a defaults helper that does **not** live in :mod:`spacr.settings`. Six built-in workflows keep their own (``foreign``, ``external_masks``, ``convert``, ``illumination``, ``barcode_qc``, ``anndata_export``), as does every plugin app, because their structured-data names are theirs alone; without this the CLI would resolve an empty defaults key-value mapping for them, and ``--set`` would then reject every one of their structured-data names as a setting that does not exist.
records.translation: ``"module:function"`` af sjálfgefinni aðstoð sem gerir **ekki** búa í :mod:`spacr.settings`. Sex innbyggð vinnuflæði geyma sín eigin (``foreign``, ``external_masks``, ``convert``, ``illumination``, ``barcode_qc``, ``anndata_export``), sem og hver viðbótarforrit, því nöfn þeirra á uppbyggðum gögnum eru þeirra einungis; án þessa myndi CLI leysa upp tóman lykil-gildi kort fyrir þau, og ``--set`` myndi þá hafna öllum nöfnum þeirra á uppbyggðum gögnum sem stillingu sem ekki er til.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.dose_response#26
records.source: R² on a sigmoid is nearly useless. Any monotone curve through a well-sampled dose–response scores above 0.95, because the total sum of squares is dominated by the difference between the two plateaus and *any* S-shaped line captures that. :meth:`DoseResponseResult.caveats` says so next to the number, every time.
records.context: R² on a sigmoid is nearly useless. Any monotone curve through a microplate sample position-sampled dose–response scores above 0.95, because the total sum of squares is dominated by the difference between the two plateaus and *any* S-shaped line captures that. :meth:`DoseResponseResult.caveats` says so next to the number, every time.
records.translation: R² á sigmoid er næstum gagnslaus. Hvaða einsleita kúrfu sem er í gegnum sýnatökustað örplatna sem er stöðluð eftir skammtasvörun fær yfir 0,95, því heildarsumma ferhyrninga er ráðandi af muninum milli tveggja flata og *hvert* S-laga lína fangar það. :meth:`DoseResponseResult.caveats` segir það við hlið tölunnar, í hvert skipti.
